experiment.name: Late-night airport expansion
experiment.question: Can airport priority and service-area expansion meet a seven-minute pickup target without overloading overnight charging?
experiment.disclaimer: Simulated output from synthetic demand. Not observed fleet performance.

demand.label: Light
demand.note: A quiet night, low end of the forecast

demand.label: Upper-tail
demand.note: A busy night, top of the forecast

dispatch.label: Demand-aware
dispatch.note: Batched min-cost assignment solved with OR-Tools

recommendation.label: Recommended
recommendation.summary: The proposed arm clears every target, including in the upper tail. Airport P90 pickup improves from 2.3 to 2.3 minutes with completion at 99.9% and charging inside its guardrail.

findings.headline: Airport P90 pickup falls to 2.3 min, inside the 7-minute target
findings.detail: Baseline sits at 2.3 min. Across replications the proposed arm's own upper tail reaches 2.3 min, so the target holds on a typical night but still holds on a hot one.

findings.headline: Trip completion rises at 99.9%
findings.detail: Baseline completes 99.8% of requests. Expansion adds demand as well as coverage, so completion holding is itself a result.

findings.headline: Charger queue stays within guardrail at 0 min in the tail
findings.detail: Median night is 0.0 min against a baseline of 0.0 min.

findings.headline: Cost per completed trip moves +2.7% to $5.48
findings.detail: Baseline is $5.34. Deadhead share moves from 14.1% to 27.1%, which is where most of the difference comes from.

guardrails: Every figure here is simulated output from synthetic demand, not observed performance.

recommendation.label: Pilot recommended
recommendation.summary: Airport P90 pickup improves from 9.8 to 7.4 minutes, which closes 24% of the gap to the 7-minute target without reaching it, and trip completion holds at 87.2%. It is not safe fleet-wide yet: under upper-tail demand the charger queue reaches 84 minutes against a 12-minute guardrail, and the constraint is charging capacity rather than dispatch. Run a staged pilot on the airport zone and two expansion zones, with charger headroom monitored nightly, before committing the full service area.

findings.headline: Airport P90 pickup improves 24% to 7.4 min, short of the 7-minute target
findings.detail: Baseline is 9.8 min. The change moves the metric substantially but does not close the gap on its own, which points at curbside capacity rather than dispatch logic as the remaining constraint.

findings.headline: Trip completion holds at 87.2%
findings.detail: Baseline completes 90.8% of requests. Expansion adds demand as well as coverage, so completion holding is itself a result.

findings.headline: Charger queue reaches 84 min in the upper tail, past the 12-minute guardrail
findings.detail: On a median night the queue is 59.1 min against a baseline of 6.1 min. The risk is concentrated in high-demand draws, when more vehicles finish the window needing charge at once.

findings.headline: Cost per completed trip moves +3.3% to $3.73
findings.detail: Baseline is $3.61. Deadhead share moves from 26.8% to 31.7%, which is where most of the difference comes from.

guardrails: Hold rollout if observed P90 charger queue exceeds 12 minutes on any pilot night.
Stage expansion zones one at a time, holding at least two weeks between additions.
Add depot charger capacity before extending the pilot to the full service area.
